statement.p: Compute the flux of the vector field \vec F = 5 y\vec i+ 4 \vec j - 5 xz\vec k through the surface S, which is the surface y=x^2+z^2, with x^2+z^2\le 9, oriented in the positive y-direction.

static.solution: y=f(x,z)=x^2+z^2, we have d\vec A=(-f_x\vec i+\vec j-f_z\vec k)\,dx\,dz= (-2x\vec i+\vec j-2z\vec k)\, dx\,dz. Thus, substituting y=x^2+z^2 into \vec F, we have \int_S \vec F\cdot d\vec A = \int_{x^2+z^2\le 9}(5 (x^2+z^2)\vec i+ 4\vec j- 5 xz\vec k)\cdot (-2x\vec i+\vec j-2z\vec k)\, dx\,dz =\int_{x^2+z^2\le 9}(-10 x^3- 10 xz^2+ 4 + 10 xz^2)\,dxdz. So \mbox{flux} = \int_{-3}^{3}\int_{-\sqrt{9-z^2}}^{\sqrt{9-z^2}}(4-10 x^3)\,dx\,dz =\int_{-3}^{3}\int_{-\sqrt{9-z^2}}^{\sqrt{9-z^2}}4\,dx\,dz - \int_{-3}^{3}\int_{-\sqrt{9-z^2}}^{\sqrt{9-z^2}}10 x^3\,dx\,dz. The first of these is just the 4 times the area of the disk, and the second is zero by symmetry, so \mbox{flux} = 4(\pi 9) = 36\pi.
